page: Microsoft Azure D2alds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Daldv6 family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical AMD EPYC 9V74 core with 2 threads per core under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz, supported by 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio.

The server includes 118 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable. In benchmark testing, the single-core performance is strong, with a stress-ng single-core score of 3078.68 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2078.0. However, multi-core performance is weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 2615.0 and a weak stress-ng multi-core result. Memory performance is also limited, with read-only small block bandwidth landing in the bottom 10% at 151.2 GB/sec, while large block write bandwidth is average at 27.75 GB/sec.

Given its low memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, this instance offers a cost-effective entry point for compute tasks that do not require large memory footprints. It is suitable for lightweight single-threaded applications, basic web serving, and simple text processing. It is less suited for memory-intensive database operations or multi-threaded compilation tasks due to its poor database operation benchmarks and weak multi-core scaling.
description: Microsoft Azure D2alds_v6 is an x86_64 server from the Daldv6 family, powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs (1 physical core, 2 threads) and 4.0 GB of system memory, establishing a compute-oriented 1:2 resource ratio. The instance includes 118 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage. Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core capabilities, highlighted by a stress-ng single-core score of 3078.68 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2078.0. Conversely, multi-core performance and memory read bandwidth are weak, with database operations scoring in the bottom 10%. This server is qualitatively cost-efficient for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic text processing, and small-scale web serving, but it is not recommended for memory-heavy databases or intensive multi-threaded tasks.
